content.title: Training & Development
content.summary: The Arvada Police Department prioritizes extensive training to enhance professionalism, accountability, and community trust among its officers and staff. With a commitment to exceeding Colorado state training requirements, the Department provides approximately 90 hours of annual in-service training, focusing on critical areas such as de-escalation, anti-bias practices, and leadership development. This continuous professional development ensures that employees are well-prepared to address the complexities of public safety effectively and ethically.
content.body:
The Arvada Police Department places a strong emphasis on training as a cornerstone of professionalism, accountability, public trust, and effective community policing. Through comprehensive and ongoing instruction, the Department ensures officers and professional staff are prepared to serve the community safely, ethically, and professionally in a rapidly evolving public safety environment.

The Department’s Training Unit oversees Department-wide training for more than 180 sworn employees and more than 70 professional staff members. Training programs are designed to meet and exceed Colorado state requirements while reflecting current best practices, legal standards, community expectations, and emerging public safety trends.

## Service Excellence Through Training

The Arvada Police Department’s training philosophy is built around the principle of "Service Excellence Through Training." The Department believes well-trained employees make better decisions, communicate more effectively, resolve conflict more safely, and provide higher levels of service to the community.

Training is not viewed as a one-time requirement, but as a continuous professional development process throughout an employee’s career.

The Training Unit is staffed by a Master Police Officer and a Police Training Coordinator who are responsible for planning, delivering, coordinating, and tracking training across the Department.

## Colorado Training Standards

Training requirements for Colorado peace officers are established by the Colorado Peace Officer Standards and Training (POST) Board, a division of the Colorado Attorney General’s Office.

Colorado POST requires peace officers to complete:

- A minimum of 24 hours of annual in-service training
- At least 12 hours in perishable skills such as:
  - Firearms
  - Defensive tactics
  - Driving skills

The Arvada Police Department significantly exceeds these minimum requirements.

In 2025, the Department provided approximately 90 hours of annual in-service training to sworn personnel,  nearly four times the state minimum requirement.

Training topics included:

- De-escalation techniques
- Crisis intervention
- Anti-bias and procedural justice training
- Leadership development
- Officer safety
- Tactical decision-making
- Legal updates
- Constitutional policing
- Communication skills
- Emergency response tactics
- Report writing and investigations

This extensive training helps ensure employees remain prepared to respond professionally and effectively to complex and evolving situations.

## Anti-Bias & Fair Policing Training

The Arvada Police Department has conducted mandatory training related to bias in policing for many years.

All sworn personnel receive ongoing instruction on topics related to fair, impartial, and constitutional policing practices. This training is designed to increase awareness of how bias can impact decision-making and community interactions while reinforcing the Department’s commitment to treating all individuals with dignity and respect.

Training topics have included:

- Implicit bias
- Cultural awareness
- Microaggressions
- Bias-based profiling
- Gender-based bias
- Disability-related bias
- Religious and ethnic bias
- LGBTQIA+ awareness
- Decision-making and perception
- Community trust and legitimacy

The Department also provides training on the social, legal, and professional impacts of biased policing practices.

While Colorado POST mandates anti-bias training every five years, the Arvada Police Department conducts this training annually as part of its ongoing commitment to professionalism and community trust.

## A Long-Term Commitment to Professionalism

Training is one of the Department’s most important long-term investments. Through ongoing professional development, realistic scenario-based instruction, leadership training, and accountability-focused education, the Arvada Police Department works to ensure employees are equipped to serve the community with professionalism, fairness, and integrity.

The Department remains committed to maintaining high standards, adapting to evolving public safety needs, and strengthening community trust through continuous learning and improvement.
